title: [finding] check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test exits 1 (a real-defect code) when a shallow clone cannot reach its pinned control commit — should be exit 3 = PREREQUISITE NOT MET; measured on two independent dispatches the same afternoon
body:
`node scripts/check-plugin-teardown-shape.mjs --self-test` exits **1** on a shallow clone, which is the same exit code a real tree defect uses. On this container every dispatched dev meets it, and the exit code alone cannot tell "the checker could not run" from "the tree is bad".

## Measured twice, independently, same afternoon

Both devs dispatched in the 2026-09-14 round hit it on their own worktrees, with no contact between them:

- **#18204's dev** — recorded it as `NOT MEASURED`, checker-health only, noting the same script's tree-judging leg exits 0.
- **#18202's dev** — cleared it by fetching the one pinned commit (`git fetch origin 621a487607881c66b2899b7e3477115229a156b4`), after which all 47 cases pass, and wrote the successor note by hand.

Two seats, two diagnoses, one cause. That cost is paid again by every dev on every card on this box.

## Cause

The self-test's positive control is pinned to a specific commit. A shallow clone cannot reach it, so the control cannot run. The script's own text names the cause and prescribes `git fetch --unshallow`.

## This is working as designed, and that is not the ask

Exiting 0 would report an unfinished self-test as a pass, which is worse; the script argues that choice in its own words and the argument is sound. ⛔ **Do not change the refusal.**

What is wrong is only the **code it refuses with**. `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` already has a distinct code for exactly this situation — **exit 3 = PREREQUISITE NOT MET**, which a dev's reconciliation classifies as NOT MEASURED rather than as a finding. The self-test's unreachable-fixture path is a prerequisite failure by that definition, and #18204's dev had to hand-classify it as one anyway.

## Ask

- When `--self-test` cannot reach its pinned control commit, exit **3**, not 1, and keep the existing message (which already names the remedy).
- Keep exit 1 for a self-test that ran and genuinely failed. The distinction is "could not run" vs "ran and was wrong".
- A one-line note beside the pin so the next reader sees why the code differs from the failure code.

Cheapest possible fix; the value is that it stops costing a diagnosis per dispatch.

## Not this card

#18180 (on a shallow checkout `git log -1 -- <path>` names a commit that never touched the path) — a different shallow-clone consequence in different code. Deduped against the last 1000 issues including closed (REST list endpoints plus local grep; `/search/*` is refused by the egress proxy by design).
